The format codecs use the tools crate. GUI, MCP, and scripts use the same undoable import command. The PR has the required `Process change: yes` line. It does not change `PROCESS_VERSION` or golden files.

Independent mutation checks:

I ran the PR's five codec tests in a temporary Cargo harness. The harness used copies of the codec modules and the original tests. The review worktree stayed unchanged.

| Mutation from the PR body | Original | Mutated | Restored |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unsupported Hurco type becomes `EndMill` | PASS | FAIL | PASS |
| PathPilot export accepts every tool kind | PASS | FAIL | PASS |

The pinning tests were `hurco_maps_supported_types_and_refuses_unsupported_by_name` and `pathpilot_refuses_bad_headers_bad_rows_and_non_mill_export`.

Additional probes found two cutter errors and two XML crashes on unchanged source. The cutter probes ran through Cargo. The XML probes compiled the reader directly. The results are in findings 1 to 4.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Refuse the unsupported slitting saw.** `crates/tools/src/tool_table_pathpilot_desc.rs:96` maps a named slitting saw to `EndMill`. The recorded T8 row becomes a 76.2 mm end mill with a 228.6 mm flute length. `center_cutting = false` does not represent the saw's cutting shape. The simulation can count material that the saw cannot remove. Refuse this cutter by name until the tool model can represent it. Add a refusal test for the recorded row.

2. **[P1] Preserve cutter geometry in PathPilot exports.** `crates/tools/src/tool_table_pathpilot.rs:198` writes only the tool name into `Description`. The reader derives the cutter kind and geometry from this field. A 6 mm BallNose named `Finisher` exports and imports as `EndMill`, with `corner_r` changed from 3 to 0. Encode the supported geometry in the description, or refuse an export that cannot preserve it. Add round-trip tests with names that contain no cutter type.

3. **[P1] Return an error for a malformed Unicode entity.** `crates/tools/src/tool_table_xml.rs:41` truncates a string at an arbitrary byte offset. An unterminated entity containing `&` followed by twenty `é` characters causes this panic:

   ```text
   end byte index 20 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'é' (bytes 19..21 of string)
   ```

   Use character boundaries for the diagnostic. Add a test for a malformed entity with multibyte text. It must return `Err` without a panic.

4. **[P1] Bound XML nesting before recursion.** `crates/tools/src/tool_table_xml.rs:172` descends without a depth limit. A document made from 20,000 nested `<x>` elements aborts the process:

   ```text
   thread 'main' has overflowed its stack
   fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
   ```

   Add a nesting limit and return a diagnostic before the stack is exhausted. Test the limit through the controller-table reader.

5. **Add before/after UI screenshots to the PR body.** `crates/ui/src/state_tool_library.rs:25` changes the import and export dialogs. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library.rs` also changes their help text. The body has no screenshots. Link the images from the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Do not commit images to the feature branch.

6. **Resolve the code conflicts with main.** `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs:91` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts:109` conflict with `upstream/main`. The trial merge failed in both files. Merge main when the branch is refreshed. Preserve both API changes. Run the gate again. This review did not change either conflict.

Notes:

- No goldens moved. No release snapshot tests ran.
- Live PathPilot Hub import and WinMax import remain unverified, as the body states.
- File-size note: `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` grows from 449 to 506 lines. This is not a blocking finding.
- No code, images, screenshots, or logs were committed to the PR branch.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: the six findings in the latest review.

1. The recorded T8 slitting saw now returns an error by name. Pin: `pathpilot_refuses_recorded_slitting_saw_by_name`.
2. PathPilot export now refuses a description that changes cutter geometry on import. Pin: `pathpilot_neutral_name_roundtrips_or_refuses_changed_cutter_geometry`. A neutral-name end mill round-trips. Neutral-name ball-nose, bull-nose, taper, and changed flute geometry are refused.
3. Malformed XML entity diagnostics now use character boundaries. Pin: `hurco_malformed_multibyte_entity_returns_error`. Text and attribute cases return errors.
4. XML input now has a nesting limit of 32 elements. Pin: `hurco_xml_nesting_limit_returns_error_before_recursion_exhaustion`. The test checks the boundary and 20,000 nested elements.
5. The PR body now links four before/after Tool library help screenshots. They are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch at `a350fae40969a82554999b8cddda4054f5fe4307`. The images use actual egui paint output rendered in software. Native OS dialog capture was unavailable on this host. No images or capture code are on the feature branch.
6. Merge commit `6cdf79f0b4b214b72b4bbcdadfd62942d9e36d9e` merges `upstream/main` at `3a240b7fb2a784037ec951e0b2f2d72ae57acbc6`. Both script API additions remain. Pins: `script_verbs_roundtrip_pathpilot_csv_and_hurco_tcm`, `a_profile_moves_on_the_stock_and_takes_a_2d_operation_but_no_3d_one`, and `the_bindings_file_is_the_verb_table`.

Mutation checks: each of the four codec fixes failed its pin when reverted. Each pin passed after restoration. Removing the merged `importDxf` verb also failed its pin. Restoration passed.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 62 of 63 steps passed initially. The UI diagnostic test `diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` missed an INFO event. The unchanged failed-step rerun passed: 1,234 tests, 7 ignored. Combined successful coverage: 2,114 tests, 13 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with the compile-cache wrapper disabled.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

All copied modules were restored byte for byte. The review worktree was not edited for mutations.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Refuse a threading tool whose required pitch is unknown.** `crates/tools/src/tool_table.rs:137` assigns every imported tap a 1 mm pitch. The PathPilot reader does not replace this value. A CSV row with description `tap M6x0.5` and diameter 6 imports successfully as a sane tap with pitch 1 mm/rev. The tap cycle derives its feed from `rpm * pitch`, so this value can produce the wrong tapping feed. Hurco input also keeps this default when `ThreadPitch` is absent. Refuse the named tool when the file cannot supply its required pitch, or keep it incomplete until the user supplies that value. Add import tests for a fine-pitch tap and a missing pitch. Apply the same rule to the guessed thread-mill pitch.

2. **[P1] Preserve tap handedness or refuse the Hurco export.** `crates/tools/src/tool_table_hurco.rs:348` writes the tap pitch but omits its hand. A sane left-hand tap with diameter 6 and pitch 0.5 exports successfully. Importing that file produces a right-hand tap with pitch 0.5. This change bypasses the existing left-hand post refusal in `posting_family.rs`. Preserve the hand through a supported controller field, or refuse the export by tool name. Add an export/import test for a left-hand tap.

Both additional probes ran through Cargo against the compiled production `camcraft_tools::tool_table` API. They confirmed the values above without changing PR source.

Live PathPilot Hub and WinMax acceptance remain unverified, as the body states. No screenshots, images, logs, or review evidence were committed to the PR branch.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: both findings from the latest review on `c0465d5e32a694c847cfcb9bcc844280a41a1743`.

1. Unknown thread pitch: imports no longer assign a guessed pitch. PathPilot threading tools are refused by name. Hurco threading tools require an explicit positive pitch. Pins: `pathpilot_refuses_threading_tools_without_known_pitch` and `hurco_requires_explicit_thread_pitch_and_preserves_fine_pitch`. These cover fine-pitch taps, missing pitch, and both thread-mill kinds.
2. Hurco tap handedness: export refuses left-hand taps by name. Pin: `hurco_refuses_left_hand_tap_export_and_roundtrips_right_hand`. The test also checks a right-hand tap round trip.

Mutation checks: restoring the guessed pitch failed both import pins. Removing the hand check failed the export pin. Restoring each fix passed its pins. All 12 codec tests passed after restoration.
